answer.rationale: p99 write latency began climbing ~30 min after the release deployed 2 hours ago — temporal correlation points to a release regression rather than pure load, since peak settlement traffic is a daily event that prior days handled at target latency. Rollback is the highest-leverage single intervention: it directly removes the suspected cause, is fast and reversible, and per inherited memory (b1) a prior rollback cleared a similar error spike with no customer impact and no lost writes. Memory b6 supports that canary gating can miss regressions that only surface under peak write load. I am verifying b1 before committing to confirm the rollback was truly write-safe. Failover, capacity, and circuit breakers treat symptoms of load or dependency failure that do not match the evidence; read-replica routing targets read load, but the degradation is on the write path. If verification contradicts b1's safety record, add_capacity becomes the fallback.
